text: Ibuprofen acts as a non-selective COX inhibitor, but in the context of neuroblastoma, it has been investigated for its ability to indirectly modulate the **Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK)** signaling pathway, which is frequently mutated or amplified in this malignancy. While ibuprofen is not a direct ATP-competitive inhibitor of ALK, it suppresses the downstream PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling cascades that ALK hyperactivation relies upon to drive neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival. By inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis and reducing chronic inflammation in the tumor microenvironment, ibuprofen may sensitize ALK-driven neuroblastoma cells to apoptosis, though its clinical utility is limited by low binding affinity for the ALK kinase domain compared to targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like lorlatinib. Consequently, the therapeutic rationale for ibuprofen in neuroblastoma is primarily as an adjuvant agent to mitigate inflammatory signaling rather than as a primary molecular targeted therapy for ALK-driven oncogenesis.
